title: Document why prefer-core-logging's stdout-safety exclusion doesn't extend to log/info/debug
description:
The `prefer-core-logging` rule excludes `console.error`/`console.warn` from its `console.* → core.*` mapping to avoid corrupting stdio protocol channels, but applies no such exclusion to `console.log`/`console.info`/`console.debug`. The issue asked whether that asymmetry is a gap or intentional.

## Finding

Intentional. The corruption risk comes from the *stream change*, not from workflow commands:

| method | writes to | replacement | writes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `console.error` / `console.warn` | **stderr** | `core.error` / `core.warning` | **stdout** (workflow command) |
| `console.log` / `console.info` | stdout | `core.info` | stdout (plain message) |
| `console.debug` (alias of `console.log`) | stdout | `core.debug` | stdout (`::debug::` command) |

For log/info/debug both sides use stdout, so the substitution cannot dirty a previously clean protocol channel — a process that owns stdout for framing is already corrupting it by calling `console.log` at all. Only the error/warn case migrates stderr traffic onto stdout.

Verified against `@actions/core`: `info()` is `process.stdout.write(message + os.EOL)`; `debug()`, `error()`, `warning()`, and `notice()` all go through `issueCommand`, which also writes to stdout.
